entries.title: Parks as crime inhibitors or generators: Examining parks and the role of their nearby context
entries.key_finding: Park effect on crime is conditional on surrounding land uses/demographics: parks can inhibit OR generate crime depending on nearby context.

entries.title: Green Space, Violence, and Crime: A Systematic Review
entries.key_finding: US evidence reviewed: results mixed overall but weight of evidence supports protective (violence-reducing) effect of urban green space.

entries.authors: Shepley M, Sachs N, Sadatsafavi H, Fournier M, Peditto K
entries.title: The Impact of Green Space on Violent Crime in Urban Environments: An Evidence Synthesis
entries.venue: International journal of environmental research and public health
entries.key_finding: 45-paper PRISMA synthesis: multiple plausible mechanisms by which green space reduces violent crime; quantitative studies mostly cross-sectional comparisons.

entries.title: Integrative Review of the Intersection of Green Space and Neighborhood Violence
entries.key_finding: 25+ studies on green space and perceived/actual safety; findings heterogeneous, safety perception improves more reliably than measured crime.
entries.design: Integrative review (25 studies: 23 quant, 5 qual, 2 mixed)

entries.authors: Branas CC, South E, Kondo MC et al. (via Asa N et al. 10-y follow-up)
entries.title: Remediating vacant lots reduces violence (Philadelphia cluster RCT) - as cited by 2026 10-year follow-up
entries.key_finding: Original 2013 cluster RCT showed short-term violence reduction; 2026 10-year follow-up re-tests sustainability with treatment assignment + longitudinal greening score.
entries.effect_size: short-term violence/crime reduction at greened lots (magnitude in full PNAS paper, not in loaded abstract)
entries.N: citywide lot RCT - N-lots not stated in abstract

entries.authors: Moyer R, MacDonald JM, Ridgeway G, Branas CC
entries.title: Effect of Remediating Blighted Vacant Land on Shootings: A Citywide Cluster Randomized Trial
entries.key_finding: Citywide cluster RCT of blight remediation on shootings in Philadelphia abstract loaded; effect estimates in full text (abstract not populated in PubMed).

entries.authors: Kondo MC, Morrison C, Jacoby SF, Branas CC
entries.title: Blight Abatement of Vacant Land and Crime in New Orleans
entries.key_finding: Quasi-experimental Fight the Blight remediation: crime changes near remediated lots mixed - some crime types shifted rather than fell (displacement-adjacent finding).

entries.authors: Jay J, Kondo MC, Lyons JG et al.
entries.title: Neighborhood segregation, tree cover and firearm violence in 6 U.S. cities, 2015-2020
entries.key_finding: In 6 cities (Baltimore, Philadelphia, Richmond, Syracuse, DC, Wilmington), race-income segregation (ICE) and tree cover both relate to shootings; green-space deficits in segregated tracts flagged as prevention target.
entries.effect_size: tree cover proportion vs shootings per tract (estimates in full text)

entries.authors: Lund JJ, Schleimer JP, Reeping PM, Pear VA et al.
entries.title: Public funds, public safety: a scoping review of government spending decisions and their impact on interpersonal violence and suicide
entries.key_finding: Scoping review of the entire government-spending/violence literature: 33 included studies; dominated by social welfare (21), health (12), education (9), law enforcement (8); community development only 2; NO library/cultural-institution spending stream identified; all ecologic designs.

entries.authors: Kagawa R et al. (Kagawa RMC, Kwong A, Smirniotis C, et al.)
entries.title: Community Safety Needs and Resources and Their Alignment: A Case Study
entries.key_finding: Cleveland 2015-2019: 1,147 safety activities in 1,625 locations coded by tract; total activities per capita POSITIVELY associated with crime frequency (RR 1.14) - i.e., resources concentrate where crime already is (composition/endogeneity echo).
entries.effect_size: RR = 1.14 activities-per-capita vs crime frequency (BYM spatial models)

entries.authors: Zhang W, Rhubart DC, Monnat SM
entries.title: Social Infrastructure Availability and Suicide Rates among Working-Age Adults in the United States
entries.key_finding: County-level availability of free social infrastructure (libraries, community centers) vs working-age suicide 2016-2019; SI framed as protective via social cohesion.
entries.design: Ecological county analysis (NVSS mortality x Natl Neighborhood Data Archive)

entries.authors: Szoko N, Ajith M, Kurland D et al.
entries.title: Community Asset Density and Past-Year Mental Health Symptoms Among Youths
entries.key_finding: Cross-sectional: density of community assets (incl. parks, libraries, schools) linked to youth mental-health symptom burden across 26 zip codes.
entries.N: 13 Allegheny County high schools, 26 zip codes

entries.authors: Langle-Chimal OD, Cadavid-Aguilar N, Meouchi-Velez A, Ponce-Lopez R
entries.title: Evaluating the reach and equity of public spaces in Mexico City using mobility data: the case of the Utopias in Iztapalapa
entries.key_finding: 13 community-center 'Utopias' network (recreation/culture/care): mobility traces + crime registry; realized access strongly patterned - composition of who uses social infrastructure drives its reach.
entries.design: Six-month mobility data + GTFS + crime registry, 13 sites

entries.authors: Pear VA, Smirniotis C, Kagawa RMC et al.
entries.title: Predicting neighborhood-level violence from features of the physical and social environment with machine learning
entries.key_finding: Cleveland/Detroit census tracts 2011-2019: XGBoost over 55 neighborhood features incl. public goods/services; environmental features predict violence - composition signal, not causal.

summary: Novelty verdict summary (PAIRING-2): Parks/green-space crime findings are VERIFICATION territory - a mature literature (Bogar & Beyer 2016; Mancus & Campbell 2018; Shepley 2019; Boessen & Hipp 2018; Branas cluster RCTs 2018/2019 + 10-y follow-up; Kondo New Orleans; Jay 2022). The parks-negative-within-city pattern is consistent with Boessen & Hipp's inhibitors-vs-generators conditioning and Kondo's mixed New Orleans results. The LIBRARY side is effectively empty: Lund 2025's scoping review of the entire government-spending/violence corpus (33 studies) contains NO library or cultural-institution spending stream; library/social-infrastructure work stops at health outcomes (Zhang 2024 suicide; Szoko 2024 youth MH). Kagawa 2026 (RR=1.14 more-activities-in-high-crime-tracts) and Pear 2025 supply the composition/endogeneity caution in neighboring form but nobody quantifies an ~80x cross-area composition gradient. => 80x-composition finding + the library-as-crime-pair = NOVEL-ANGLE (library half near-GAP); parks within-city counter-trend = VERIFIED-with-nuance. UK/EU-specific replication: not found (gap).
